title: Saturday Night Queue
description: Reservation code must atomically enforce capacity, purchase idempotency and outbox insertion. Hold expiry is application logic; asynchronous DynamoDB TTL deletion is not a booking clock. The Streams-to-bus element aggregates an EventBridge Pipe and its configured target. Consumers tolerate duplicate events, lag and version changes. The mail worker and connection details are omitted. The illustrated global-table replica is read-only by application/IAM policy, not an inherently read-only DynamoDB service mode. Failover needs fencing of the old writer, reconciliation and an explicit sales-resumption decision. CloudFront/WAF are global account resources; Cognito, SQS and DynamoDB are regional. Edge login arrows show browser identity progression. The audit arrow summarizes a separately configured pipeline, not Lambda writing directly across accounts without permission.

edges.meaning: WAF web ACL is associated with the distribution; not an extra request proxy hop.
Browser starts user-pool login; identity data is not cached as site content.
Browser presents scoped access token; authorizer verifies issuer and audience.
Authenticated booking command; server validates event, buyer and purchase limits.
Transactional conditional capacity update and outbox record; application expiry, not TTL deletion, releases holds.
DynamoDB Streams feed a configured EventBridge Pipe with duplicate-tolerant processing.
Filter committed purchases; do not independently dual-write from reservation code.
Door-list projection can lag and must deduplicate event versions.
Independent delivery queue decouples email work from the reservation transaction.
Configured SQS redrive after failed consumer attempts; mail worker is omitted from this projection view.
Asynchronous global-table replica is read-only by application policy; no active-active capacity allocation.
Audit pipeline records sensitive booking actions in a separate account; transport and KMS policies require implementation.
